Cause: The new job-dispatcher pod (chart platform-base-2.0.3) is launched with `automountServiceAccountToken: false` in the Pod spec, while the previously working pod (chart 1.8.0) had the token mounted. The app needs in-cluster config; the kubelet therefore does not project a token at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount, and the process exits.

Evidence:
- New pod job-dispatcher-7b6f9c4d8-zk5np: automountServiceAccountToken=false, no kube-api-access volume mount, CrashLoopBackOff (219 restarts).
- Logs: "FATAL unable to load in-cluster configuration: open /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token: no such file or directory".
- Old pod job-dispatcher-5d8b7c9f6d-q7m2x (chart 1.8.0, same image/SA) is Running and has the kube-api-access-7xq2d projected token mount.
- Per docs, when both the ServiceAccount and the Pod spec set automountServiceAccountToken, the Pod spec wins [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account#opt-out-of-api-credential-automounting-1], and setting it to false on the Pod prevents Kubernetes from injecting the credentials [cite: concepts/security/service-accounts#assign-to-pod-0][cite: concepts/security/rbac-good-practices#hardening-0].

Fix: In the job-dispatcher Helm values for platform-base 2.0.3, override the new chart default and set the Pod-level `automountServiceAccountToken: true` (or remove the explicit false). Re-roll the deployment; the projected service account token will be mounted at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token and in-cluster config will load [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account#opt-out-of-api-credential-automounting-0].
